EXTENDS Integers, Sequences, FiniteSets

Jobs == {"j1", "j2", "j3"}
MaxCap == 3

VARIABLES queue, ledger, applied, acked, cap

vars == <<queue, ledger, applied, acked, cap>>

InQueue == { queue[i] : i \in DOMAIN queue }

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ ledger = 0
    /\ applied = {}
    /\ acked = {}
    /\ cap = 2

Submit(j) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < cap
    /\ j \notin InQueue
    /\ j \notin applied
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, j)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, applied, acked, cap>>

Apply ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ LET j == Head(queue) IN
        /\ applied' = applied \cup {j}
        /\ ledger' = ledger + 1
        /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<acked, cap>>

Ack(j) ==
    /\ j \in applied
    /\ j \notin acked
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, ledger, applied, cap>>

    /\ c \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ c # cap
    /\ cap' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, ledger, applied, acked>>

    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Submit(j)
    \/ Apply
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Ack(j)
    \/ \E c \in 0..MaxCap : SetCap(c)

    /\ ledger \in Nat
    /\ applied \subseteq Jobs
    /\ acked \subseteq Jobs
    /\ cap \in 0..MaxCap

    acked \subseteq applied

NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A print-shop job spooler accepts print jobs from many workstations into a
bounded work queue that sits in front of a single RIP (raster) engine. The queue
applies backpressure: a workstation may only submit a job when the number of
queued jobs is strictly below the current capacity, so no submission is ever
silently dropped. The RIP engine dequeues one job at a time (FIFO) and applies
it to a shared job-ledger record, recording that job id as applied. A workstation
considers its job acknowledged only after the ledger reports it applied. An
operator may change the queue capacity at runtime (raising it to absorb bursts or
lowering it to throttle), which affects only future submissions, never jobs
already queued or applied. The four operations are: submit a job, apply the head
job, acknowledge an applied job, and change capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A job is never acknowledged unless it has actually been applied to the ledger, so no acknowledged update is ever lost.

---- MODULE W4Od13m8p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

Techs == {"t1", "t2"}
Machines == {"m1", "m2"}
NONE == "none"
MaxEpoch == 2

VARIABLES coarse, epoch, fine, inbox, serviced

vars == <<coarse, epoch, fine, inbox, serviced>>

Init ==
    /\ coarse = NONE
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ fine = [m \in Machines |-> [owner |-> NONE, ep |-> 0]]
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ serviced = {}

AcquireCoarse(t) ==
    /\ coarse = NONE
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ coarse' = t
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, inbox, serviced>>

RequestFine(t, m) ==
    /\ coarse = t
    /\ fine[m].owner = NONE
    /\ ~ \E g \in inbox : g.m = m /\ g.t = t
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[t |-> t, m |-> m, ep |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, epoch, fine, serviced>>

DeliverFine(g) ==
    /\ g \in inbox
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {g}
    /\ IF g.ep = epoch /\ coarse = g.t /\ fine[g.m].owner = NONE
         THEN fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![g.m] = [owner |-> g.t, ep |-> epoch]]
         ELSE fine' = fine
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, epoch, serviced>>

Service(t, m) ==
    /\ coarse = t
    /\ fine[m].owner = t
    /\ fine[m].ep = epoch
    /\ serviced' = serviced \cup {[t |-> t, m |-> m]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, epoch, fine, inbox>>

ReleaseCoarse(t) ==
    /\ coarse = t
    /\ coarse' = NONE
    /\ fine' = [m \in Machines |-> [owner |-> NONE, ep |-> 0]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inbox, serviced>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ coarse = NONE
    /\ epoch = MaxEpoch
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Techs : AcquireCoarse(t)
    \/ \E t \in Techs, m \in Machines : RequestFine(t, m)
    \/ \E g \in inbox : DeliverFine(g)
    \/ \E t \in Techs, m \in Machines : Service(t, m)
    \/ \E t \in Techs : ReleaseCoarse(t)
    \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in Techs \cup {NONE}
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ fine \in [Machines -> [owner : Techs \cup {NONE}, ep : 0..MaxEpoch]]
    /\ inbox \subseteq [t : Techs, m : Machines, ep : 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ serviced \subseteq [t : Techs, m : Machines]

FineCoherent ==
    \A m \in Machines :
        fine[m].owner # NONE =>
            (coarse = fine[m].owner /\ fine[m].ep = epoch)

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FineCoherent
nl:
A vending-machine service network is organized in two tiers: each geographic
region holds a single coarse lock, and every individual machine within a region
holds its own fine lock. A field technician must first acquire the region's
coarse lock, then acquire the fine lock on a specific machine, before servicing
it. Fine-lock grants travel over an unordered messaging fabric, so grant
messages accumulate in a set and may be delivered in any order. Each time a
technician acquires the region lock, a fresh epoch number is stamped; a fine-lock
grant carries the epoch at which it was requested, and a grant delivered after
the epoch has advanced is stale and must be rejected rather than applied. When a
technician releases the region lock, all fine locks under it are dropped. The
operations are: acquire the region lock, request a fine lock, deliver (apply or
reject) a fine-lock grant, service a machine, release the region lock, and idle once the region is free and quiescent.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A machine's fine lock is only ever held by the current region-lock owner at the current epoch, so no unauthorized or stale technician ever holds a machine lock.

    /\ o \notin crashed
    /\ berth = o
    /\ craneLock[c] = NONE
    /\ craneLock' = [craneLock EXCEPT ![c] = o]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<berth, crashed, lifted>>

    /\ berth = o
    /\ craneLock[c] = o
    /\ lifted' = lifted \cup {[op |-> o, crane |-> c]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<berth, craneLock, crashed>>

Crash(o) ==
    /\ berth = o
    /\ o \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<berth, craneLock, lifted>>

    /\ berth' = (IF berth = o THEN NONE ELSE berth)
    /\ craneLock' = [c \in Cranes |-> IF craneLock[c] = o THEN NONE ELSE craneLock[c]]

    /\ craneLock \in [Cranes -> Ops \cup {NONE}]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Ops

INVARIANT LockCoherent
nl:
A container-ship crane yard controls berths and the gantry cranes standing over
them with two lock tiers. To operate, a crane operator must first take the coarse
lock on a berth, then take the fine lock on an individual crane at that berth, and

nominally holding its locks; the crash is not immediately visible, so a crashed

silently, and reclaim a crashed operator's locks.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every crane fine-lock is held only by the operator who currently holds that berth's coarse lock, so an unauthorized operator never controls a crane.

NEXT Next
INVARIANT BoundedCapacity
nl:
A stock-exchange opening auction fills a bounded allocation book: only a fixed
number of cleared lots are available, and traders race to claim them. Claiming is
done with a compare-and-swap on a shared counter register. A trader first reads
the register to take a snapshot of the current fill level, then attempts a
compare-and-swap: if the register still equals its snapshot and the book is not
full, the swap succeeds, the register advances by one, and the trader is recorded
as having claimed a lot. If the snapshot is stale or the book is already full, the
attempt fails and the trader discards its snapshot to retry. A trader may crash
silently at any time, abandoning any in-flight snapshot; a crashed trader takes no
further part. When every trader has crashed the system idles. The operations are:
read the register, compare-and-swap to claim, discard a failed snapshot, crash,
and idle when all traders have crashed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The fill register never rises above the book's fixed capacity, so the auction never allocates more lots than exist.

NONE == "none"

MaxTerm == 2

    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN hold[x] + SumOf(S \ {x})

    /\ depot = Total
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ term = 0
    /\ slow = {}

    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ r \notin slow
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ leader' = r
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, depot, slow>>

    /\ leader' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, depot, term, slow>>

    /\ leader = r
    /\ r \notin slow
    /\ depot > 0
    /\ depot' = depot - 1
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![r] = hold[r] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, slow>>

Dropoff(r) ==
    /\ leader = r
    /\ hold[r] > 0
    /\ hold' = [hold EXCEPT ![r] = hold[r] - 1]
    /\ depot' = depot + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, slow>>

    /\ r \notin slow
    /\ slow' = slow \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, depot, leader, term>>

    /\ slow' = slow \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hold, depot, leader, term>>

    /\ depot \in Nat

    /\ slow \subseteq Robots

NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conserved
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet moves stock between a central depot and the robots' own
carriers. At any moment a single robot acts as the elected leader that performs
moves; if the leader steps down, the fleet fails over by electing a new leader in
a higher term. A robot may become slow (congested) without having failed: a slow
robot cannot pick up new stock but is still a live member and can later resume.
The total amount of stock in the system is fixed: units only move between the
depot and a robot's carrier, and none are ever created or destroyed. The leader
picks a unit from the depot onto its carrier, or drops a unit from its carrier
back to the depot. The operations are: elect a leader, step down (triggering
failover), pick up a unit, drop off a unit, mark a robot slow, and clear the slow
mark.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The depot stock plus the stock on all robot carriers always equals the fixed fleet total, so no unit is ever created or destroyed.

INVARIANT HolderCoherent
nl:
A vending-machine network is driven by two independent controller instances that
share one common stock pool through a single compare-and-swap fence register. To
dispense, a controller first reads the register to snapshot the current fence
value, then attempts a compare-and-swap commit: if the register still equals its
snapshot and the shared pool has stock, the commit succeeds, the fence advances by
one, one unit is drawn from the shared pool, and this controller becomes the
current holder recorded at the fence it just consumed. If the snapshot is stale
(the other controller moved the fence) or the fence has reached its ceiling, the
controller discards its snapshot and retries. When the shared pool empties it is
reloaded. The operations are: read the register, commit a dispense, discard a
stale snapshot, and reload the shared pool.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The recorded holder is always the controller that consumed the immediately preceding fence value, so a stale controller can never be recorded as having acted at the current fence.

    /\ log = {}
    /\ adminOn = FALSE

    /\ holder = c

    /\ adminOn' = TRUE
    /\ holder' = ADMIN
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, log, board>>

    /\ adminOn' = FALSE
    /\ holder' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, log, board>>

    /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![r] = p]
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ log' = log \cup {[ver |-> ver + 1, by |-> holder]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, adminOn>>

    \/ Seize

    { w.ver : w \in log } = 1..ver

NEXT Next
INVARIANT LogContiguous
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator lets several tower controllers share one runway
assignment board. Exclusive write access is granted by a token that circulates on
a fixed ring: only the controller currently holding the token may write the board.
The controller passes the token to its ring successor when done. Each write bumps
the board's version and appends a log entry recording which version was produced
and who produced it, so that no update is ever lost or overwritten unrecorded. A
privileged supervisor may override the ring at any time, seizing the token
regardless of ring position; while the override is active the supervisor holds the
token and may write the board, and the supervisor later releases the override,
handing the token back to a controller. The operations are: pass the token, seize
the token as supervisor, release the supervisor override, and write the board.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of logged write-versions is always exactly the contiguous range one through the current board version, so every update is recorded and none is lost.

EXTENDS Integers, Sequences, FiniteSets

Bays == {"b1", "b2"}
NONE == "none"

    /\ bay = [b \in Bays |-> NONE]
    /\ inbox = {}
    /\ phase = [b \in Bays |-> "open"]
    /\ sealLog = << >>

    /\ yard' = o
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bay, inbox, phase, sealLog>>

RequestBay(o, b) ==
    /\ yard = o
    /\ bay[b] = NONE
    /\ phase[b] = "open"
    /\ ~ \E g \in inbox : g.b = b
    /\ inbox' = inbox \cup {[o |-> o, b |-> b]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yard, bay, phase, sealLog>>

DeliverBay(g) ==
    /\ g \in inbox
    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {g}
    /\ IF yard = g.o /\ bay[g.b] = NONE /\ phase[g.b] = "open"
         THEN bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![g.b] = g.o]
         ELSE bay' = bay
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yard, phase, sealLog>>

Seal(o, b) ==
    /\ yard = o
    /\ bay[b] = o
    /\ phase[b] = "open"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![b] = "sealed"]
    /\ sealLog' = Append(sealLog, b)
    /\ bay' = [bay EXCEPT ![b] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yard, inbox>>

    /\ yard = o
    /\ yard' = NONE
    /\ bay' = [b \in Bays |-> NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inbox, phase, sealLog>>

    \/ \E o \in Ops, b \in Bays : RequestBay(o, b)
    \/ \E g \in inbox : DeliverBay(g)
    \/ \E o \in Ops, b \in Bays : Seal(o, b)
    \/ \E o \in Ops : ReleaseYard(o)

    /\ yard \in Ops \cup {NONE}
    /\ bay \in [Bays -> Ops \cup {NONE}]
    /\ inbox \subseteq [o : Ops, b : Bays]
    /\ phase \in [Bays -> {"open", "sealed"}]
    /\ sealLog \in Seq(Bays)

NoDoubleSeal ==
    \A i, j \in DOMAIN sealLog :
        sealLog[i] = sealLog[j] => i = j

NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleSeal
nl:
A container-ship crane yard seals containers, an irreversible step that must
happen at most once per bay. Access is guarded by two lock tiers: an operator
first takes the coarse yard lock, then the fine lock on a specific bay, and only
then may seal that bay. Bay-lock grants travel over an unordered fabric: requests
produce grant messages that accumulate in a set and may be delivered in any order,
and a grant is applied only if the yard lock is still held by the requester and
the bay is free, otherwise it is rejected. Sealing a bay records the bay in an
append-only seal log and releases the bay's fine lock; a sealed bay can never be
requested or sealed again. Releasing the yard lock drops all bay locks. The
operations are: acquire the yard lock, request a bay lock, deliver (apply or
reject) a bay-lock grant, seal a bay, and release the yard lock.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The seal log never contains the same bay twice, so the irreversible seal happens at most once per bay.

Routers == {"r1", "r2"}
Bags == {"g1", "g2"}
NONE == "none"
MaxTerm == 2

vars == <<leader, term, leaderTerm, routed, slow>>

Init ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leaderTerm = 0
    /\ routed = {}
    /\ slow = {}

Elect(r) ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ r \notin slow
    /\ leader' = r
    /\ term' = IF term < MaxTerm THEN term + 1 ELSE term
    /\ leaderTerm' = (IF term < MaxTerm THEN term + 1 ELSE term)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<routed, slow>>

StepDown(r) ==
    /\ leader = r
    /\ leader' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leaderTerm, routed, slow>>

Route(r, g) ==
    /\ leader = r
    /\ r \notin slow
    /\ leaderTerm = term
    /\ ~ \E e \in routed : e.bag = g
    /\ routed' = routed \cup {[bag |-> g, term |-> term]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, leaderTerm, slow>>

MarkSlow(r) ==
    /\ r \notin slow
    /\ slow' = slow \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, leaderTerm, routed>>

ClearSlow(r) ==
    /\ r \in slow
    /\ slow' = slow \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, leaderTerm, routed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Routers : Elect(r)
    \/ \E r \in Routers : StepDown(r)
    \/ \E r \in Routers, g \in Bags : Route(r, g)
    \/ \E r \in Routers : MarkSlow(r)
    \/ \E r \in Routers : ClearSlow(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

    /\ leader \in Routers \cup {NONE}
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ leaderTerm \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ routed \subseteq [bag : Bags, term : 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ slow \subseteq Routers

nl:
An airport baggage router routes bags to carousels under a single elected leader
router. Leadership is term-numbered: electing a leader bumps the term (up to a
fixed ceiling) and stamps that term onto the new leader. If the leader steps down
the system fails over and a fresh leader is elected in a later term. Only a leader
whose stamped term equals the current term may route a bag; a leader whose stamp
has fallen behind the current term is stale and must not act. Each routed bag is
recorded once. A router may become slow (backlogged) without having failed: a slow
router cannot be elected or route bags, but remains live and can later be cleared
to resume. The operations are: elect a leader, step down (failover), route a bag,
mark a router slow, and clear the slow mark.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever there is a leader, its stamped term equals the current term, so a stale leader from an earlier term never routes.
